input: page-sheet.json only. Chosen before any prose is written.

sections.why: States the page's one claim: your network has an inside, an outside, and one door. Short, sets up the picture.
The reader runs real commands on their own machine. Code is the only honest form for commands.
Three reserved ranges with what they look like at home. Lookup-shaped content.

The visual need is spatial: devices inside a subnet, a router with two sides, the internet outside. The diagram block is a linear list and cannot show two sides of a boundary, so an authored figure is used.
The apartment analogy explains subnet and router jobs in one connected story.
Three jobs, each with what it does and where you see it. Parallel rows.
One request out and back is a strict sequence. This is exactly what the linear diagram is for.
One right answer: which address is local.
The reader writes down their own values, which the rest of the series reuses.
Private ranges and NAT behavior come from standards; link them.
Points to listeners on one machine.

rejected.why: No warning on this page earns one.
